subject: B
topic: UNESCO World Heritage Sites (Standalone Special Test)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In which year did the UNESCO General Conference adopt the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage (popularly called the 'World Heritage Convention')?
questions.explanation: The World Heritage Convention was adopted by the UNESCO General Conference in 1972 and provides the legal framework for identifying and protecting sites of Outstanding Universal Value. 1945 is when UNESCO itself was founded, not the Convention. 1965 saw only preliminary international discussions, with no convention adopted. 2003 is when UNESCO adopted the separate Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, which is a different treaty altogether.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the UNESCO World Heritage programme:

(i) A property must possess Outstanding Universal Value (OUV) to be inscribed.
(ii) India is a permanent member of the World Heritage Committee.
(iii) World Heritage properties are grouped into cultural, natural and mixed categories.
(iv) The World Heritage Committee is composed of 21 States Parties.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Outstanding Universal Value is the core criterion for inscription. Statement (iii) is correct — sites are classified as cultural, natural or mixed. Statement (iv) is correct — the Committee has 21 members drawn from States Parties. Statement (ii) is incorrect — there are NO permanent members; the 21 members are elected for fixed terms, so no country holds a permanent seat. Hence only (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Taj Mahal was among the very first Indian properties inscribed on the World Heritage List.
Reason (R): The Taj Mahal was inscribed in 1983, the same year in which Agra Fort, the Ajanta Caves and the Ellora Caves also entered the List.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Taj Mahal was one of India's earliest inscriptions. Reason (R) is correct — India's first four sites were all inscribed in 1983: the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta Caves and Ellora Caves. Because the 1983 batch is exactly what made the Taj one of the first, (R) directly explains (A). Option B is wrong because (R) does explain (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is factually correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following World Heritage Sites in India with the states in which they are located:

Column I:
(a) Kaziranga National Park
(b) Khajuraho Group of Monuments
(c) Group of Monuments at Hampi
(d) Sun Temple, Konark

Column II:
(i) Madhya Pradesh
(ii) Odisha
(iii) Assam
(iv) Karnataka

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park is in Assam (a-iii). Khajuraho is in Madhya Pradesh (b-i). Hampi is in Karnataka (c-iv). The Sun Temple, Konark, is in Odisha (d-ii). Option A wrongly places Khajuraho in Karnataka and Hampi in Madhya Pradesh. Option B wrongly places Kaziranga in Karnataka. Option D swaps Hampi and Konark, placing Hampi in Odisha and Konark in Karnataka, both of which are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are inscribed as NATURAL World Heritage Sites in India?

(i) Sundarbans National Park
(ii) Western Ghats
(iii) Great Living Chola Temples
(iv) Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans (i), the Western Ghats (ii) and Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers (iv) are all inscribed as natural sites for their biodiversity and ecosystems. The Great Living Chola Temples (iii) are a CULTURAL site (temple architecture of the Chola dynasty), not a natural one, so every option containing (iii) is wrong. Hence only (i), (ii) and (iv) are natural sites.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is India's only 'mixed' World Heritage Site, recognised for both natural and cultural significance?
questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim (inscribed 2016) is India's only mixed site, valued for its Himalayan biodiversity and for the sacred cultural traditions associated with Mount Khangchendzonga. Kaziranga, Nanda Devi and the Sundarbans are all inscribed purely as NATURAL sites for their ecosystems and wildlife, not as mixed sites, so they do not qualify.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The city of __________ became the first city in India to be declared a UNESCO World Heritage City, in 2017. Fill in the blank: __________
questions.explanation: The Historic City of Ahmedabad (the walled old city) was inscribed in 2017 and became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City. Jaipur was inscribed as a World Heritage City later, in 2019, so it was not the first. Delhi has several individual monuments on the List but has not been inscribed as a World Heritage City. Hyderabad is not a World Heritage City at all.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the World Heritage List:

(i) The first sites were inscribed on the List in 1978.
(ii) UNESCO's headquarters, which administers the List, is located in Geneva.
(iii) The Galápagos Islands were among the first sites inscribed in 1978.
(iv) Cultural criteria are numbered (i) to (vi) and natural criteria (vii) to (x).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the first 12 sites were inscribed in 1978. Statement (iii) is correct — the Galápagos Islands were in that first 1978 batch. Statement (iv) is correct — criteria (i)–(vi) are cultural and (vii)–(x) are natural. Statement (ii) is incorrect — UNESCO's headquarters is in PARIS, not Geneva. Hence only (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which national park, a natural World Heritage Site, is famous for sheltering about two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinoceros?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park in Assam (inscribed 1985) protects the largest population of the great one-horned rhinoceros. Gir National Park is famous for the Asiatic lion, not the rhino. Jim Corbett and Ranthambore are celebrated for the Bengal tiger; neither is a rhino habitat nor a natural World Heritage Site, so Kaziranga is the only correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following world-famous World Heritage Sites with the countries in which they are located:

Column I:
(a) Machu Picchu
(b) Angkor
(c) Petra
(d) Great Barrier Reef

Column II:
(i) Cambodia
(ii) Australia
(iii) Peru
(iv) Jordan

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu is in Peru (a-iii), Angkor is in Cambodia (b-i), Petra is in Jordan (c-iv) and the Great Barrier Reef is in Australia (d-ii). Option B wrongly places Machu Picchu in Jordan and Petra in Peru. Option C wrongly places Angkor in Jordan and Petra in Cambodia. Option D wrongly places Machu Picchu in Cambodia and Angkor in Peru.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Italy has among the highest number of World Heritage Sites of any country in the world.
Reason (R): The very first site ever inscribed on the World Heritage List was the Colosseum in Rome.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Italy consistently tops or nearly tops the country ranking of World Heritage Sites. Reason (R) is incorrect — the first sites were inscribed in 1978 (such as the Galápagos Islands and Aachen Cathedral); the Colosseum is part of the Historic Centre of Rome, which was inscribed in 1980, and was never the very first site. So (A) is correct but (R) is false. Options A and B are wrong because they claim (R) is correct, and option D is wrong because it claims (A) is false.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: As of the 2025 (47th) session, India had 44 World Heritage Sites. Of these, 7 are natural sites and 1 is a mixed site. How many of India's World Heritage Sites are purely cultural?
questions.explanation: The cultural sites equal the total minus the natural and mixed ones: 44 − 7 (natural) − 1 (mixed) = 36 cultural sites. The value 35 results from wrongly subtracting an extra site, 37 from ignoring the single mixed site (44 − 7), and 38 from ignoring the mixed site and miscounting the natural ones. Only 36 matches the correct arithmetic.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following World Heritage Sites in India is a celebrated group of rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments known for its murals and sculptures?
questions.explanation: The Ajanta Caves in Maharashtra (inscribed 1983) are rock-cut Buddhist caves famous for their paintings and sculpture. The Elephanta Caves are predominantly Hindu (Shaivite) cave temples, not Buddhist. The Bhimbetka Rock Shelters are prehistoric shelters known for Stone Age paintings, not carved cave monasteries. The Bagh Caves, though Buddhist, are not inscribed as a World Heritage Site.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's World Heritage Sites:

(i) The Sun Temple at Konark is located in Odisha.
(ii) The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram is in Tamil Nadu.
(iii) The Rani-ki-Vav (Queen's Stepwell) is in Rajasthan.
(iv) The Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus is in Mumbai.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — Konark's Sun Temple is in Odisha. Statement (ii) is correct — Mahabalipuram is in Tamil Nadu. Statement (iv) is correct — Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus is in Mumbai. Statement (iii) is incorrect — Rani-ki-Vav is at Patan in GUJARAT, not Rajasthan. Hence only (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are inscribed as CULTURAL World Heritage Sites in India?

(i) Qutb Minar and its Monuments
(ii) Great Himalayan National Park
(iii) Rani-ki-Vav
(iv) Fatehpur Sikri

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Qutb Minar (i), Rani-ki-Vav (iii) and Fatehpur Sikri (iv) are all cultural sites recognised for their architecture and history. The Great Himalayan National Park (ii) is a NATURAL site inscribed for its biodiversity, not a cultural one, so any option containing (ii) is wrong. Hence only (i), (iii) and (iv) are cultural sites.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which railway was the first to be inscribed under the World Heritage Site titled 'Mountain Railways of India'?
questions.explanation: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway was inscribed first, in 1999, and the site was later extended. The Nilgiri Mountain Railway was added in 2005 and the Kalka–Shimla Railway in 2008, so neither was first. The Kangra Valley Railway is a scenic mountain line but has never been part of the 'Mountain Railways of India' World Heritage Site.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of World Heritage Sites inscribed for India in selected years:

1983 → 4
1985 → 3
1986 → 4
1987 → 3

Based only on this data, in which listed year(s) did India receive the highest number of inscriptions?
questions.explanation: The highest value in the data is 4, which occurs in both 1983 (Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora) and 1986 (Khajuraho, Hampi, Fatehpur Sikri, Goa Churches). '1983 only' and '1986 only' each ignore the other year that also had 4 inscriptions. '1985 and 1987' both had only 3 inscriptions, which is not the highest, so that option is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Kaziranga National Park is a natural World Heritage Site.
Reason (R): Assam is a state situated in north-eastern India.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Kaziranga is a natural World Heritage Site (inscribed 1985). Reason (R) is also correct — Assam does lie in north-eastern India. However, a park's geographic location in the north-east does not explain WHY it earns natural World Heritage status; that comes from its biodiversity and rhino habitat. So both statements are true but (R) is not the explanation of (A). Option A is wrong because (R) does not explain (A), and options C and D are wrong because both statements are actually true.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Great Living Chola Temples, a World Heritage Site comprising temples such as the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, are located primarily in which state?
questions.explanation: The Great Living Chola Temples are in Tamil Nadu, built by the Chola dynasty and including the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur. Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka each have their own heritage temples but the Chola temples of this inscribed group lie in Tamil Nadu, so those three states are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about world-famous World Heritage Sites:

(i) The Great Wall is a World Heritage Site located in China.
(ii) The Statue of Liberty is a World Heritage Site in the United States.
(iii) Stonehenge is located in France.
(iv) The Acropolis of Athens is in Greece.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the Great Wall is in China. Statement (ii) is correct — the Statue of Liberty is in the United States. Statement (iv) is correct — the Acropolis is in Athens, Greece. Statement (iii) is incorrect — Stonehenge is in the UNITED KINGDOM, not France. Hence only (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Indian World Heritage Sites with their year of inscription:

Column I:
(a) Taj Mahal
(b) Jaipur City
(c) Dholavira
(d) Moidams (Ahom mound-burial system)

Column II:
(i) 2019
(ii) 1983
(iii) 2024
(iv) 2021

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal was inscribed in 1983 (a-ii), Jaipur City in 2019 (b-i), Dholavira in 2021 (c-iv) and Moidams in 2024 (d-iii). Option A wrongly gives Jaipur 2021 and Dholavira 2019. Option C wrongly gives the Taj Mahal 2019 and Jaipur 1983. Option D swaps the years of Dholavira and Moidams, giving Dholavira 2024 and Moidams 2021, both incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which body takes the final decision to inscribe a property on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
options: The UNESCO General Assembly of all member states
questions.explanation: The World Heritage Committee, made up of 21 States Parties, meets annually and decides which nominated sites are inscribed. The UN Security Council deals with international peace and security, not heritage. The General Assembly of States Parties elects the Committee but does not itself inscribe sites. The International Court of Justice is the UN's principal judicial organ and has no role in inscription.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are World Heritage Sites situated in Delhi, India's national capital?

(i) Qutb Minar
(ii) Humayun's Tomb
(iii) Red Fort
(iv) Charminar

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Qutb Minar (i), Humayun's Tomb (ii) and the Red Fort Complex (iii) are all World Heritage Sites located in Delhi. The Charminar (iv) is in Hyderabad, Telangana, and is not on the World Heritage List, so any option containing (iv) is wrong. Hence only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The prehistoric __________ Rock Shelters in Madhya Pradesh, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are famous for their ancient cave paintings dating back to the Stone Age. Fill in the blank: __________
questions.explanation: The Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh (inscribed 2003) are renowned for their prehistoric paintings and evidence of early human habitation. The Bagh Caves are Buddhist rock-cut caves, not prehistoric shelters. Udayagiri Caves are early Hindu/Jain rock-cut caves. The Barabar Caves are ancient rock-cut caves in Bihar. None of these three fits a prehistoric painted rock shelter in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Serengeti National Park, a famous natural World Heritage Site known for the great wildebeest migration, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: The Serengeti National Park is in Tanzania (inscribed 1981) and is celebrated for the annual migration of wildebeest and zebra. Kenya's adjoining reserve is the Maasai Mara, which is a different, separately managed area. South Africa's flagship park is Kruger, and Botswana's is Chobe/Okavango — none of these is the Serengeti, so Tanzania is the only correct answer.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about World Heritage Sites in India:

(i) The Hill Forts of Rajasthan (a group of forts such as Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh) are inscribed as a World Heritage Site.
(ii) The Jantar Mantar in Jaipur is a World Heritage Site.
(iii) Kaziranga National Park lies in West Bengal.
(iv) Kaziranga National Park is protected mainly for the one-horned rhinoceros.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the Hill Forts of Rajasthan were inscribed in 2013. Statement (ii) is correct — the Jantar Mantar, Jaipur, was inscribed in 2010. Statement (iv) is correct — Kaziranga is protected chiefly for the one-horned rhino. Statement (iii) is incorrect — Kaziranga is in ASSAM, not West Bengal. Hence only (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Jammu and Kashmir currently has three inscribed UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Reason (R): To be inscribed, a property must demonstrate Outstanding Universal Value and be formally nominated by the State Party concerned.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is incorrect — Jammu and Kashmir has no inscribed World Heritage Site so far; some sites appear only on India's tentative list. Reason (R) is correct — inscription genuinely requires Outstanding Universal Value and a nomination by the State Party. So (A) is false while (R) is true. Options A and B are wrong because they claim (A) is correct, and option C is wrong because (R) is actually correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 47th session (2025) of the World Heritage Committee, at which India's 44th site was inscribed, was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: The 47th session was held in Paris, France, in July 2025, where the Maratha Military Landscapes of India became India's 44th site. Busan, Republic of Korea, hosted the later 48th session in 2026. New Delhi hosted the 46th session in 2024. Fuzhou, China, chaired the 44th session in 2021. Hence Paris is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of new sites inscribed on the World Heritage List in recent sessions:

46th session (2024) → 24
47th session (2025) → 26
48th session (2026) → 25

Based only on this data, which session recorded the highest number of new inscriptions?
questions.explanation: The highest figure in the data is 26, recorded at the 47th session in 2025. The 46th session (2024) had 24 and the 48th session (2026) had 25, both fewer than 26, so those options are wrong. The 46th (24) and 48th (25) were not equal to each other, so that option is also incorrect. Only the 47th session is the highest.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: At the end of the 47th session (2025), the World Heritage List had 1,248 sites. At the 48th session (2026), 25 new sites were inscribed and none were removed. How many sites were on the List after the 48th session?
questions.explanation: Adding the new inscriptions: 1,248 + 25 = 1,273 sites. The value 1,270 comes from wrongly adding only 22, 1,248 wrongly assumes no additions at all, and 1,298 comes from mistakenly adding 50 (double counting). Only 1,273 matches the correct addition of 25 new sites to the previous total.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following, a Harappan-era city in Gujarat, was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2021?
questions.explanation: Dholavira, a Harappan city in the Kutch region of Gujarat, was inscribed in 2021 as 'Dholavira: A Harappan City'. Lothal is another Harappan port site in Gujarat but is only on India's tentative list. Kalibangan is a Harappan site in Rajasthan, not inscribed. Rakhigarhi in Haryana, though a major Harappan site, is likewise not a World Heritage Site.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are World Heritage Sites in India associated primarily with Buddhist heritage?

(i) Mahabodhi Temple Complex, Bodh Gaya
(ii) Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi
(iii) Khajuraho Group of Monuments
(iv) Nalanda Mahavihara (ruins of Nalanda University)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya (i), the Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi (ii) and the ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara (iv) are all Buddhist heritage sites. The Khajuraho Group of Monuments (iii) consists mainly of Hindu and Jain temples, not Buddhist ones, so any option containing (iii) is wrong. Hence only (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian component of the transnational World Heritage Site 'The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier' is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The Capitol Complex in Chandigarh is India's component of the 2016 transnational inscription of Le Corbusier's architecture. Although Le Corbusier designed some buildings in Ahmedabad too, only the Chandigarh Capitol Complex is part of the inscribed World Heritage Site. Mumbai and Puducherry have their own heritage but no Le Corbusier component on the List.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following properties was actually delisted (removed) from the UNESCO World Heritage List?
questions.explanation: The Dresden Elbe Valley in Germany was delisted in 2009 after a road bridge was built across the valley, damaging its Outstanding Universal Value — showing that sites CAN be removed. The Historic Centre of Rome and the Old City of Jerusalem remain on the List, while the Kathmandu Valley, though placed on the 'in Danger' list at times, was never delisted. Hence only the Dresden Elbe Valley was removed.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following natural World Heritage Sites with the countries in which they are located:

Column I:
(a) Galápagos Islands
(b) Yellowstone National Park
(c) Kilimanjaro National Park
(d) Sagarmatha National Park

Column II:
(i) United States
(ii) Nepal
(iii) Ecuador
(iv) Tanzania

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: The Galápagos Islands are in Ecuador (a-iii), Yellowstone is in the United States (b-i), Kilimanjaro National Park is in Tanzania (c-iv) and Sagarmatha (Everest) National Park is in Nepal (d-ii). Option A wrongly places Kilimanjaro in Nepal and Sagarmatha in Tanzania. Option B wrongly places the Galápagos in the USA and Yellowstone in Ecuador. Option D wrongly places the Galápagos in Tanzania and Kilimanjaro in Ecuador.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following was inscribed as India's 43rd World Heritage Site in 2024?
options: Moidams – the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty
questions.correctAnswer: Moidams – the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty
questions.explanation: Moidams in Assam were inscribed in 2024 as India's 43rd World Heritage Site, and the first from the north-east in the cultural category. Santiniketan and the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were both inscribed earlier, in 2023, as India's 41st and 42nd sites. The Ramappa Temple in Telangana was inscribed in 2021, so none of these three is the 43rd site.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: In the context of World Heritage inscription, what does the abbreviation 'OUV' stand for?
questions.explanation: OUV stands for Outstanding Universal Value, the central concept a site must demonstrate to be inscribed on the World Heritage List. 'Official UNESCO Verification' is not a real UNESCO term. 'Overall Universal Viability' and 'Outstanding Unique Variety' are invented expansions that sound plausible but are not used in the World Heritage framework, so only the first option is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about World Heritage Sites:

(i) The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system and a natural World Heritage Site.
(ii) The Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu is inscribed as a mixed World Heritage Site.
(iii) The Pyramids of Giza are located in South Africa.
(iv) Angkor is a World Heritage Site in Cambodia.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement (i) is correct — the Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system and a natural site. Statement (ii) is correct — Machu Picchu is inscribed as a mixed (cultural and natural) site. Statement (iv) is correct — Angkor is in Cambodia. Statement (iii) is incorrect — the Pyramids of Giza are in EGYPT, not South Africa. Hence only (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Keoladeo National Park, a World Heritage Site famous as a bird sanctuary and wintering ground for migratory birds, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Keoladeo National Park (formerly the Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary) is in Rajasthan and was inscribed in 1985 for its rich birdlife, including migratory waterfowl. Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana each have wildlife areas of their own, but Keoladeo specifically lies near Bharatpur in Rajasthan, so those three states are incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 46th session of the World Heritage Committee (2024) was hosted, for the first time ever, by which country?
questions.explanation: India hosted the 46th session of the World Heritage Committee in New Delhi in July 2024 for the first time in its history. China hosted the 44th session (Fuzhou, 2021), France hosted the 47th session (Paris, 2025) and also houses UNESCO's headquarters, while Saudi Arabia hosted the 45th session (Riyadh, 2023). Hence India is the correct answer.
